The Translators' Hebrew OT follows the Qere because this  is what most translations use - including the KJV. THe Ketiv is recorded as a Variant. 																
																
FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:																
==============																
Ref in Heb (Eng)	Hebrew Bible versification (with Eng in brackets when different. Word numbers according to divisions spaces and metheg, as in Ketiv.   Eng Ref is based on KJV which is followed by almost all English versions. Occasionally a verse break is in a different place - i.e. Num.26.1; 1Sa.21.1; 1Ki.18.33; 20.3; 22.22; 22.43; 1Ch.12.4; Isa.64.1; and all Psalm Titles.															
Text type:	The text follows  T (the text in BHS/Leningrad as pointed by the Masoretes), unless M (Masorete corrections in the margin and elsewhere) change the meaning) or O (other texts, notably LXX) add words commonly translated in modern BIbles). A letter in brackets - eg (T) or  (O) refers to a variant.															
	The Qere is the scribal version in the margin and the Ketiv is the version found in the main text (if it is unpointed, the pointed version has been produced by Westminster and occasionally corrected by Tyndale scholars). Translations tend to follow the Qere, incl KJV and most modern translations.															
Hebrew	Pointing, cantillation and punctuation, following the Qere with the Ketiv as a variant when the meaning differs. The Qere follows those listed by Westminster.															
	Divisions ( / ) separate  prefixes, suffixes and punctuation. These are mirrored in the transliteration, translation, lexical tagging and grammar. 															
	Hebrew is derived from Westminster Leningrad text WLC 4.20 via OpenScriptures, with occasional corrections towards the Leningrad Codex by BHS or by Tyndale scholars. It is, essentially, a corrected version of BHS. 															
English translation:  	The divisions "/" missor the divisions in Hebrew. Words in <angle brackets> are in the Hebrew but are best not  included in a translation. Words in [square brackets] aren't in the Hebrew but are implied and are best included in a translation. 															
dStrongs = Lexical = Gloss	Lexical tags for each element of the Hebrew, including punctuation, separated by " /" with the Root tag in {curly brackets}. Each is made up of a  disambiguated Strong number (dStrong - as defined at TinyURL.com/STEP-Disambiguated), the lexical form in Heberew, and an English gloss with the sub-meaning after " » " where appropriate. 															
Grammar	Morphology is from ETCBC, with Ketiv forms parsed by Tyndale scholars - see e.g. Deu.33.2-15.   For the source of ETCBC and conversion method by Tyndale House, see https://goo.gl/yKaXQq#HebMorph2															
	Morphology codes follow the form defined by OpenScriptures at http://openscriptures.github.io/morphhb/parsing/HebrewMorphologyCodes.html#vt															
Meaning variant	All Ketiv variants (K) with a different grammar or vocabulary are noted, with occasional significant variants from Aleppo (A), Ben Chaim (C),  Masorah Itture Sopherim (I) other Hebrew variants (V), alternate word divisions (D)															
Conjoin word																
sStrong+Instance	Simple Strongs (sStrongs) are the numbers found in simpler tagged BIbles - ie without the prefixes, suffixes or disambiguation. 															
	Instances mark more than one occurrence of the same sStrong in the same verse: "_A" is appended for the 1st instance  (eg G1234_A), "_B" for the 2nd instance etc.  A lower case (eg "_b") indicates the word may not be included in some tagged Bibles, because it is not found in all manuscripts or because there is also an alternate way to tag this word. 															
Alt Strongs	Alternate ways to tag the same word using Strongs tags. Differences are usually due to different interpretations of the Hebrew root.  	The purpose of this and the sStrong+Instance is to help line up this data with other tagged Bibles.  														
																
																
																
Strongs numbers are augmented (with additions of "a", "b" etc) in line with BDB based on OpenScriptures																
 and extended into the 9000s to include prefixes & suffixes - as in TBESH - Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs for Hebrew at https://STEPBible\.github.io/STEPBible-Data/																
 §numbers represent submeanings within the Strongs number,  added by Tyndale scholars (not fully checked)																
 §names represent unique names for people, places and other proper nouns such as months etc.  as in TIPNR - Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References at https://STEPBible\.github.io/STEPBible-Data/
